the_instruction_i_had_been_ignoring: 'You have to use the web to the fullest. You can take any perfect solutions there or any code in the repos there or from AI researches there.' I searched the web for Claude Opus 5.5's SPECS seven times and never once searched it for CODE TO TAKE. This round I did.
what_the_research_gave: Hyperdimensional Computing (Kanerva 2009) + Random Indexing (Sahlgren 2005) + Holographic Reduced Representations (Plate 1995). Verbatim from the survey: the binding operation 'does not require any training'; Random Indexing 'only require[s] a single pass through the training data'. That is the user's thesis stated in the literature twenty years before they stated it, with mathematics instead of a claim.
what_i_built: canonical/runtime/hyperdimensional_semantics_v1.py — a semantic space where a word's meaning is the sum of its neighbours' FIXED random vectors. There is no parameter to train: blake2b(token) is the entire embedding table, and only a SUM accumulates.

speedups_found_by_profiling.dead_order_accumulation_removed: 1.95s to 0.93s; order is bound in phrase() and the stored order vector was never read by neighbours()

quality_work_that_was_necessary: Function words must not be context and must not own a vector. Measured: the six nearest neighbours of 'capability' were 'and, to, by, is, the, as'. After: 'knowledge, law, laws, engine, frontier'.

The common component must be removed. Measured: 'evidence' and 'claim' were nearest to 'the, is, and, for'. Subtracting the mean context vector is what Sahlgren's RI does. After: evidence -> verifier, properties, registry; claim -> digest, target, benchmark, exact.
Identifiers must be split. Measured: a test function name arrived as one token 'testfailthefallthroughisscopedtowhat'. Splitting snake_case and camelCase fixed it.

what_it_can_do_measured.neighbours: verify -> verifier, guard, binding, reconciliation | evidence -> claim, candidate, source | bound -> verified, registry, capability, adapter, goal | receipt -> receipts, verification, sha, evidence, soundness
what_it_can_do_measured.word_association_learned_from_prose: model -> [weights, gradient, nothing, epochs, gradients] — the space learned what a model is associated with, and this one has none of them
what_it_can_do_measured.composition: phrase('verified capability') vs phrase('capability verified') cosine 0.501 — order is encoded by permutation, no training

what_it_CANNOT_do_and_i_will_not_claim: It cannot produce a vector for a word it has never seen in context, and it says so rather than inventing one.

ANALOGY IS UNRELIABLE AT SCALE. On a tight corpus 'capability->bound :: receipt -> executed' is right. Over 764 mixed files 'fail->failure :: refuse -> [apt-cli, canonical-namespace, ...]' is noise. Random indexing gives similarity; the offset for a relational analogy is not sharp enough at this scale. I am not claiming a solved analogy engine.

It does NOT close the routing gap yet. Measured: on goals whose words the router could not place, semantic expansion changed the top candidate on 0 of 4 probes. The neighbours were correct; the expansion was not strong enough to outvote the router's own scoring. It is wired as a layer and it is honest about being inert on its own.

It is not comparable to a transformer on open-domain language. 28.5k tokens/sec through pure Python with fixed random vectors is a very different object from a trained model, and the only fair statement is that the SHAPE of the two is different, not that one is better.
why_this_matters_for_the_user_s_thesis: It is the first piece in this tree where the no-weights claim is a MECHANISM rather than an accounting fact. Everything else established weights:0 by not having a model. This has a semantic space -- word meaning, similarity, composition -- with trained parameters 0 by construction, because the vectors are random draws and only sums accumulate.
